text: [curious] Algebra... is named after an Arabic word for setting broken [shouting] BONES!
Algebra is named after an Arabic word for setting broken [shouting] BONES!
Al-jabr: putting broken pieces back together, like setting a bone.
Around the year 820, in Baghdad, al-Khwarizmi wrote the book on solving equations by al-jabr.
Europe translated it into Latin, and al-jabr became: algebra.
In Spain, a bone-setter was even called an algebrista!
And al-Khwarizmi's own name? It became the word algorithm.
Your turn. Between the two sujood, the Prophet, peace be upon him, used to ask Allah:
And MEND me! Set right whatever is broken in me.
What do you say between the two sujood? Comment below!
Europe turned al-jabr into algebra... and al-Khwarizmi's own name into algorithm.
Your turn. Between the two sujood, the Prophet, peace be upon him, asked:
Algebra is named after an Arabic word for... setting broken bones.
